newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait union considers Ahmadi oil export strike.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait union considers Ahmadi oil export strike.

text.p: A Kuwaiti oil workers' union said on Wednesday it was considering a possible strike at the Mina al-Ahmadi oil export terminal.
Kuwait National Petroleum Co (KNPC) labour union chairman Hamad al-Souyan told Reuters the union would meet at 1300 (1000 GMT) to discuss the possible strike with the chairman of KNPC.
But exports of crude and refined products were still flowing out of Ahmadi, Souyan said.

About 120 workers out of 919 at Ahmadi, which has a 420,000 barrels per day refinery and an oil export terminal, have asked the union to help in a dispute with KNPC over its promotion system, Souyan said.
"If there was no solution there will be a strike," he said.
"It is not in the union's policy to resort to strike," Souyan said. "(But) the nature of Kuwaiti unions is that if any union declares a strike is seeks expanding it to make it work."
"We hope to solve the problem in today's meeting," he said. "A strike does not serve the economic situation."
KNPC is the refining arm of the state-owned oil conglomerate Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC).
In March 1995 the Kuwait Oil Co (KOC) labour union launched a strike aimed at halting Kuwait's three percent share of world production to demand a reshuffle of employment grades.
